purpose: Patiromer is used to lower high potassium levels in your blood, a condition called hyperkalemia. High potassium can be dangerous because it can affect how your heart beats. Your doctor may prescribe this if your kidneys are not removing enough potassium on their own.
how_it_works: Patiromer works in your gut like a sponge — it grabs onto extra potassium in your intestines and holds onto it so your body cannot absorb it. The potassium then leaves your body naturally through your stool. This helps bring your potassium levels down to a safer range.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include constipation, diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, and gas. Some people may also notice low magnesium levels in their blood, so your doctor will check this with blood tests.
warnings: Take patiromer at least 3 hours apart from other medications you take by mouth, because it can bind to other medicines and make them less effective. Do not use this medication if you have a blockage in your bowel. Tell your doctor if you have any history of bowel problems. Always follow up with blood tests as your doctor recommends to monitor your potassium and magnesium levels.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one packet (8.4 grams) mixed with water and taken by mouth once a day with food. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your blood potassium levels. Always mix it well and drink the full amount. Never heat the mixture or take it as a dry powder.
